text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 30 in history.
1691 - Robert Boyle, British chemist noted for his experiments on the properties of gases, died.
1865 - Rudyard Kipling, English novelist, short-story writer and poet, born in India, where his novels "Kim" and "The Jungle Book" are set.
1879 - Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera "The Pirates of Penzance" premiered in Paignton, England.
1880 - The Transvaal, under Paul Kruger, declared itself a republic.
1884 - Hideki Tojo, Japanese soldier, born. Prime minister of Japan during most of World War Two, he was hanged as a war criminal in December 1948.
1894 - Amelia Jenks Bloomer, U.S. women's rights campaigner, died. She invented "bloomers" in 1850.
1903 - A fire in the Iroquois Theatre in Chicago killed 588 people; public outrage led to new theatre safety codes across America.
1906 - Carol Reed, English film director best known for the film adaption of Graham Greene's "The Third Man" and the Oscar-winning musical "Oliver", born.
1915 - Four hundred people died when the Germans torpedoed the British P & O liner Persia off Crete.
1916 - Grigory Rasputin, Siberian peasant, mystic, and favourite of Tsar Nicholas II and Tsarina Alexandra, murdered.
1922 - The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was established through the confederation of Russia, Byelorussia, Ukraine and the Transcaucasian Federation.
1947 - King Michael of Romania was forced to abdicate when the Romanian People's Republic was proclaimed.
1968 - Trygve Lie, Norwegian statesman and first secretary-general of the United Nations (1946-52), died.
1979 - U.S. composer Richard Rodgers died; he collaborated with Oscar Hammerstein II in the hit musicals "Oklahoma!", "South Pacific", "The King and I" and "The Sound of Music".
1985 - President Zia-ul-Haq of Pakistan ended martial law, in operation since he came to power in 1977.
1988 - Yugoslav Prime Minister Branko Mikulic and his government resigned in an economic policy showdown with parliament.

1988 - President Ronald Reagan and president-elect George Bush were subpoenaed to testify at the trial of former White House aide Oliver North on criminal charges stemming from the Iran-Contra affair.
1988 - Yury Churbanov, son-in-law of former Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev, was jailed for 12 years for bribery.
1992 - Bulgaria's parliament approved Lyuben Berov as prime minister.
1992 - Interim Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani was elected head of state for two years in a ballot in which he was the sole candidate.
1993 - Sudan, angered by the Archbishop of Canterbury's visit to the rebel-held south, ordered the British ambassador to leave the country.
1995 - Tens of thousands of cheering Palestinians greeted PLO leader Yasser Arafat in Ramallah in the West Bank after Israeli troops withdrew from the city.
1995 - Hundreds of people, many weeping with joy, lined the streets of Gorazde in eastern Bosnia to welcome the first passenger bus into the Moslem enclave for over three years.
